images.filename: Entering the Canadian War Museum proper (24748079242).jpg
images.caption: We finally enter the Canada War Museum. After getting our tickets, we need to enter a glass door and walk down this long and narrow corridor to the main exhibition hall. The Canadian War Museum (CWM) (French: Musée canadien de la guerre) is Canada's national museum of military history. Located in Ottawa, Canada, the museum covers all facets of Canada's military past, from the first recorded instances of death by armed violence in Canadian history several hundred years ago to the country's most recent involvement in conflicts. It includes major permanent exhibitions on wars that have been fought on Canadian soil, the total wars of the twentieth century, the Cold War and peace support operations abroad, and Canada's history of honouring and remembrance. There is also an open storage area displaying large objects from the Museum's collection, from naval guns to tanks, from motorcycles to jet aircraft. The exhibits depict Canada's military past in its personal, national and international dimensions. (Ottawa, Canada, June 2015)

images.caption:
At Paardeberg, the Royal Canadian Regiment first attacked on 18 February 1900. Accurate Boer fire forced them to take cover. Broiling in the hot sun, this soldier trapped in the open, has found partial protection behind a large ant-hill.
By the time the South African War began in 1899, the British Army had abandoned its familiar red coats for the camouflage of khaki uniforms. The infantry carried a standard .303 Lee-Enfield Mk. I rifle. Canadians added the maple leaf badge to the covered cork helmet.

images.caption:
Model for the National War Memorial
In 1926, this model by British sculptor Vernon March won the competition for Canada’s First World War memorial in Ottawa. Twenty-two uniformed figures pass through an arch bearing the allegorical figures of Peace and Freedom.

images.caption:
As with most museums I have visited I will only show you a small part of what there is to see. It would be easy to spend a couple of days here.
The Canadian War Museum is Canada's national museum of military history. The museum covers all parts of Canada's military history, from armed violence in Canadian history several hundred years ago to the country's most recent involvement in conflicts. It has many permanent exhibitions on wars that have been fought on Canadian soil, the total wars of the twentieth century, the Cold War and peace support operations abroad, and Canada's history of honouring and remembrance. There is also a large storage area displaying large objects from the Museum's collection, from naval guns to tanks, from motorcycles to jet aircraft.
